pamphlet_excerpts: Differences Between Continuous Tone Line: The halftone dots are so small, the human eye cannot see the individual dots unless they are magnified, but the eye does see anoverall effect (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 2: The arrangement of the halftone dots creates this effect (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 3: The halftone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look dark are big and fill most of the halftone dot area (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 4: The halftone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look light are small and fill very little of thehalftone dot area (p. 44).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): Generally, halftones are made from a continuous-toneimage, such as a traditional photograph (p. 44).
Step 2 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): In the past, thecontinuous-tone image was photographed through a specialscreen that created a halftone version of the original (p. 44).
Step 3 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): Today it is more common to take a continuous-tone image and scan it into a computer or to take a picture with a digital camera (p. 44).
Step 4 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): Thecomputer software then converts the digital file into a pattern ofsmall halftone dots that make up an image (p. 44).

Make a layout, and produce a plate using a process approved by your counselor. Run the plate and print at least 50 copies. (b) Screen printing. Make a hand-cut or photographic stencil and attach it to a screen that you have prepared. Mask the screen and print at least 20 copies. Resource: Screen Printing Tutorial (video) (c) Electronic/digital printing. Create a layout in electronic form, download it to the press or printer, and run 50 copies. If no electronic interface to the press or printer is available, you may print and scan a paper copy of the layout. (d) Relief printing. Create a layout in electronic form, download it to the press or printer, and run 50 copies. If no electronic interface to the press or printer is available, you may print and scan a paper copy of the layout.
